# Problem 1

```{r message=FALSE}
library(p8105.datasets)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

data("ny_noaa")
```

```{r include=FALSE}
skimr::skim(ny_noaa)
```

## NY NOAA Data Description

1. The `ny_noaa` dataset contains 2,595,176 daily observations from 747 stations (1981–2010), with seven variables: `id`, `date`, `prcp`, `snow`, `snwd`, `tmax`, and `tmin`.

2. Missing rates are highest for `tmax` and `tmin` (43.71% each), followed by `snwd` (22.80%), `snow` (14.69%), and `prcp` (5.62%). Station IDs and dates are complete.


## Data Cleaning

```{r}
ny_noaa_clean =
  ny_noaa |>
  separate(
    date,
    into = c("year", "month", "day"),
    sep = "-"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(year),
    month = as.numeric(month),
    day = as.numeric(day),
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = prcp / 10,
    snow = snow / 10,
    snwd = snwd / 10
  )
```

```{r include=FALSE}
ny_noaa_clean |>
  count(snow, name = "n_obs") |>
  arrange(-n_obs) |>
  head(10)
```

1. The date was separated into numeric `year`, `month`, and `day` variables. Temperatures were converted to degrees Celsius, precipitation to millimeters, and snowfall and snow depth to centimeters.

2. The most common value is 0 cm. Common positive values include 1.3, 2.5, and 5.1 cm, consistent with measurements in approximate half-inch and whole-inch increments.


## Average Maximum Temperatures

```{r}
monthly_tmax_df =
  ny_noaa_clean |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) |>
  drop_na(tmax) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax),
    n_days = n()
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    month = case_when(
      month == 1 ~ "January",
      month == 7 ~ "July"
    )
  )


monthly_tmax_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .25, size = .7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(. ~ month) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Maximum Temperature by Station and Year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Mean maximum temperature (C)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

1. January is substantially colder than July. Mean maximum temperatures vary across stations and years.

2. Some station-year averages are extreme, including approximately -13.4°C in January and 33.6°C in July. These values should be examined alongside the number of recorded days.


## Temperature and Snowfall Distributions

```{r}
ggp_temp =
  ny_noaa_clean |>
  drop_na(tmax, tmin) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_bin2d(bins = 50) +
  labs(
    title = "Maximum vs Minimum Temperature",
    x = "Minimum temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum temperature (C)",
    fill = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggp_snow =
  ny_noaa_clean |>
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(year), y = snow)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "blue", alpha = .7) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    breaks = c("1981", "1985", "1990", "1995", "2000", "2005", "2010")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Positive Snowfall Distribution by Year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Snowfall (cm)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggp_temp / ggp_snow
```

1. Maximum and minimum temperatures are strongly positively associated. However, 1,183 complete observations have `tmax < tmin`, suggesting possible data inconsistencies.

2. Positive snowfall distributions are right-skewed across years, with most observations concentrated at smaller amounts.








# Problem 2

## Data Cleaning

```{r}
nhanes_covar_df =
  readxl::read_excel(
    "./data/nhanes_covar.xlsx",
    skip = 4,
    na = c("", "NA")
  ) |>
  janitor::clean_names()

nhanes_accel_df =
  readxl::read_excel("./data/nhanes_accel.xlsx") |>
  janitor::clean_names()
```

```{r}
nhanes_covar_df =
  nhanes_covar_df |>
  filter(age >= 21) |>
  drop_na(sex, age, bmi, education) |>
  mutate(
    sex = case_when(
      sex == 1 ~ "Male",
      sex == 2 ~ "Female"
    ),
    education = case_when(
      education == 1 ~ "Less than high school",
      education == 2 ~ "High school equivalent",
      education == 3 ~ "More than high school"
    ),
    sex = factor(
      sex,
      levels = c("Male", "Female")
    ),
    education = factor(
      education,
      levels = c(
        "Less than high school",
        "High school equivalent",
        "More than high school"
      )
    )
  )
```

```{r}
nhanes_accel_tidy =
  nhanes_accel_df |>
  pivot_longer(
    min1:min1440,
    names_to = "minute",
    names_prefix = "min",
    values_to = "mims"
  )


nhanes_df =
  left_join(
    nhanes_covar_df,
    nhanes_accel_tidy,
    by = "seqn"
  ) |>
  group_by(seqn) |>
  mutate(
    minute = min_rank(
      factor(minute, levels = str_c(1:1440))
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    seqn = factor(seqn)
  )
```

1. Participants younger than 21 or with missing demographic data were excluded. Sex and education were converted to factors.

2. The cleaned dataset contains 228 participants and 328,320 minute-level observations.



## Demographic Summary

```{r}
nhanes_covar_df |>
  count(education, sex) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = n
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
nhanes_covar_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = sex, y = age, fill = sex)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_grid(. ~ education) +
  labs(
    title = "Age Distribution by Sex and Education",
    x = "Sex",
    y = "Age (years)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

1. The sample includes 118 men and 110 women. The largest education group is "More than high school", with 115 participants.

2. Participants with more than a high school education tend to be younger. The age distributions of men and women overlap within each education group.


## Total Daily Activity

```{r}
nhanes_total_df =
  nhanes_df |>
  group_by(seqn, age, sex, education) |>
  summarize(
    total_mims = sum(mims)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

nhanes_total_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = total_mims, color = sex)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(. ~ education) +
  labs(
    title = "Total Daily Activity by Age, Sex, and Education",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Total daily MIMS",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

1. Total daily activity was calculated by summing the 1,440 minute-level MIMS values for each participant.

2. The fitted lines show a decrease in total activity with age across all three education groups. Activity levels vary considerably, with no consistent difference between men and women across education groups.


## 24-Hour Activity Patterns

```{r}
nhanes_time_df =
  nhanes_df |>
  mutate(
    hour = (minute - 1) / 60
  ) |>
  group_by(education, sex, hour) |>
  summarize(
    mean_mims = mean(mims)
  ) |>
  ungroup()


nhanes_time_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = hour, y = mean_mims, color = sex)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(. ~ education) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(0, 6, 12, 18, 24)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "24-Hour Activity Patterns by Sex and Education",
    x = "Hour of Day",
    y = "Mean MIMS per Minute",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

1. Activity levels are lowest overnight and increase during the morning. They remain relatively high during the day before decreasing in the evening.

2. Men and women show similar daily patterns across education groups, although their average activity levels differ somewhat.







# Problem 3

## Data Cleaning

```{r}
citi_jan_2020 =
  read_csv("./data/Jan 2020 Citi.csv") |>
  mutate(
    year = 2020,
    month = "January"
  )

citi_july_2020 =
  read_csv("./data/July 2020 Citi.csv") |>
  mutate(
    year = 2020,
    month = "July"
  )

citi_jan_2024 =
  read_csv("./data/Jan 2024 Citi.csv") |>
  mutate(
    year = 2024,
    month = "January"
  )

citi_july_2024 =
  read_csv("./data/July 2024 Citi.csv") |>
  mutate(
    year = 2024,
    month = "July"
  )
```

```{r}
citi_df =
  bind_rows(
    citi_jan_2020,
    citi_july_2020,
    citi_jan_2024,
    citi_july_2024
  ) |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = c("January", "July")
    ),
    weekdays = factor(
      weekdays,
      levels = c("Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday") ),
    member_casual = factor(
      member_casual,
      levels = c("casual", "member")
    ),
    rideable_type = factor(
      rideable_type,
      levels = c("classic_bike", "electric_bike")
    )
  )
```

1. The combined dataset contains 99,485 rides from January and July of 2020 and 2024, with 9 variables describing ride information, duration, stations, membership status, and bike type.

2. Each row represents one ride. Month, weekday, membership status, and bike type were converted to factors.

3. Missing values occur only in station names, with 43 missing starting stations and 207 missing ending stations.


## Ride Counts

```{r}
citi_df |>
  count(year, month, member_casual) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = member_casual,
    values_from = n
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

1. Members account for more rides than casual riders in all four months.

2. Ride counts are higher in July than in January for both years. Both membership groups also have more rides in 2024 than in the corresponding months of 2020.


## Top 5 Starting Stations in July 2024

```{r}
citi_df |>
  filter(year == 2024, month == "July") |>
  drop_na(start_station_name) |>
  count(start_station_name, name = "n_rides") |>
  arrange(-n_rides) |>
  head(5) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Pier 61 at Chelsea Piers was the most popular starting station in July 2024, with 163 rides in the sample.


## Median Ride Duration by Weekday, Month, and Year

```{r}
citi_median_df =
  citi_df |>
  group_by(year, month, weekdays) |>
  summarize(
    median_duration = median(duration)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

citi_median_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = weekdays, y = median_duration)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(aes(group = 1)) +
  facet_grid(year ~ month) +
  labs(
    title = "Median Ride Duration by Weekday, Month, and Year",
    x = "Day of Week",
    y = "Median ride duration (minutes)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

1. Median ride durations are longer in July than in January for both years. Rides are also generally longer in 2020 than in 2024.

2. Weekend rides tend to be longer than weekday rides, especially in July. This pattern is less clear in January 2024.
